title: Introduce 'cost-accordion' prefill controller, telemetry hooks, and quant hint translator
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a tenant-aware prefill controller (Cost Accordion) that dynamically adjusts prefetch size based on workload elasticity, exposes new telemetry for prefill economics, and introduces a quant hint translator to generate safe per-tenant quant profiles. Includes a CLI dry-run for cost simulation and docs.
description:
Motivation: We need safer, tenant-scoped automation for prefill/batching defaults and quantization hints so customers get predictable unit economics without manual tuning. The Cost Accordion is a lightweight controller that widens or narrows prefill windows based on short-term demand elasticity, observed KV-cache hit patterns, and tenant budget tier. The quant hint translator converts tenant-level policies (e.g., prefer int8 when p99 latency budget allows) into per-model quant profiles with conservative fallbacks to avoid regressions. This PR bundles runtime logic, telemetry, a CLI dry-run, and docs so operators can preview changes before rollout.

What changed (high level): implemented accordion controller in the prefill service, added telemetry events and histograms to capture prefill size distribution and unit-econ delta, implemented quant_hint_translator library with safety gates, added a console toggle and dry-run CLI to simulate tenant-level policy effects, and included integration tests + perf microbenchmarks.

Checklist: - [x] Accordion controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Quant hint translator + policy-to-profile mapping - [x] Telemetry hooks and metric names (prefill.size_histogram, prefill.unit_econ_delta, quant.hint_applied_count) - [x] CLI dry-run (redwood cli cost accordion --dry-run) - [x] Console UI flag and doc pages - [x] Integration tests and CI perf smoke - [x] Backwards-safe defaults and conservative fallbacks

Commits summary: 1) 9f3c2d6 - prefill: add cost accordion controller with basic windowing and backoff heuristics; 2) 4a1b7e2 - telemetry: emit prefill.size_histogram and unit_econ_delta events; 3) c6d9f81 - optimizer: add quant_hint_translator with policy->profile mapping and safety checks; 4) 2b7e3aa - cli: add cost-accordion dry-run command; 5) 7d4a0ff - console: add toggle and preview panel; 6) a11b22c - tests: integration + perf microbench; 7) b9c3f44 - docs: write cost-accordion.md and update upgrade notes.

Files changed (summary): ["services/prefill/accordion.go", "services/prefill/accordion_test.go", "optimizer/quant_hint_translator.py", "optimizer/quant_hint_profiles/README.md", "telemetry/prefill_metrics.proto", "telemetry/emitters/prefill_emitter.go", "cli/cost_accordion_cli.go", "console/src/components/CostAccordionPreview.tsx", "docs/cost-accordion.md", "docs/upgrade-notes-2026-02.md", "tests/integration/prefill_accordion_integration.test"]

Testing and perf: unit tests cover window sizing logic and safety fallbacks. Integration test suite simulates tenant traffic curves (burst, steady, spiky) and asserts no regression on p99 latency with default conservative policy. Perf microbench (CI job) measured token throughput with accordion enabled vs. baseline; observed 6-9% token-cost reduction under bursty workloads and <2% p99 latency change at targeted SLOs for our synthetic tenant mix. CI initially flaked on a telemetry histogram aggregation test under high concurrency; rerun after tightening a test timeout and mock emitter fixed flakiness.

Review conversation (high level): - Ethan: "Can you add a short explanation in docs about how the fallback quant profile is chosen? Also please include unit-econ examples for a small and large tenant." Reply (Maya): "Added section and two example tables to docs/cost-accordion.md; included CLI sample outputs for dry-run." - Lina: "Telemetry names look good, but let's keep metrics backward-compatible. We should prefix new histograms with 'prefill.'" Reply: "Renamed metrics to prefill.* and updated emitters and dashboards references." - Omar: "Please ensure controller respects tenant overrides and does not modify pinned tenants." Reply: "Controller checks for tenant.pin_prefill and tenant.quant_lock; when set, controller is read-only for that tenant. Added tests." - Eduardo (SRE): "How safe is the quant hint translator? Any guardrails to avoid quality regressions?" Reply: "Translator includes a canary threshold: it applies only when historical eval pass-rate >= 98% for the requested quantization and will fall back to fp16 if latency gains are marginal. Documented behavior in optimizer/quant_hint_profiles/README.md."

Rollout plan: merge to main, ship to staging behind feature flag, run 48h canary across two mid-size tenants, enable telemetry dashboards and the CLI dry-run for operators to experiment. If unit-econ regressions >5% or p99 latency >SLO, auto-disable accordion for affected tenants.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps default behavior conservative (accordion starts at default prefill=2 and will not exceed 8 unless unit-econ delta demonstrates >6% token cost savings without p99 regressions). The code path for pinned/premium tenants is opt-in via tenant policy so enterprise customers retain deterministic behavior.
